text: The 50 t exemption is now described as it is in law: all CBAM goods an importer brings in during a calendar year count towards one 50 t, not each good separately.
Imports dated 2027 and 2028 are now tested against the 50 t exemption. The calculator had treated it as a 2026-only rule; the law sets no end date.
The fallback default value for origins without their own figure is now described correctly: it is set from the ten exporting countries with the highest emission intensities, not a world average.
The certificate price is now described as quarterly for 2026 and weekly from 2027.
Imports dated 2027 and 2028 now count certificates. No price is published for those years yet, so no euro figure is shown.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740 corrects the default values in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621, applying from 1 January 2026.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 sets the default emission values for the definitive period.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2620 sets the benchmarks used to deduct free allocation from certificates.
Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 simplifies CBAM: an annual 50 t exemption per importer, and certificate sales from 1 February 2027.
